summary: Subnetwork prod-shared-vpc-us-east1 (10.20.0.0/20) has VPC Flow Logs disabled (enableFlowLogs=false), leaving traffic to/from resources in this subnet unobserved for network forensics and any diagnostics that depend on flow-log data.

evidence.detail: no VpcFlowLogsConfig entry targets prod-shared-vpc-us-east1 (only prod-shared-vpc-us-central1-flow-logs, targeting the us-central1 subnet, was found)

reasoning.description: Subnetwork prod-shared-vpc-us-east1's own enableFlowLogs field is false, meaning Compute Engine's built-in per-subnet flow-log toggle is off.

No Network Management API VpcFlowLogsConfig targeting this subnet exists either (see observability-reference.gcp-flow-logs-us-central1.json, which covers only the sibling us-central1 subnet), confirming no flow-log mechanism -- built-in or Network Management API -- is active for prod-shared-vpc-us-east1.

assumptions: No project-level or organization-level default flow-log policy overrides this subnet's own enableFlowLogs setting.
limitations: This finding evaluates flow-log configuration only; it does not check whether another observability mechanism (e.g. Packet Mirroring) provides equivalent coverage for this subnet.
remediation: Enable flow logs on subnetwork prod-shared-vpc-us-east1 (gcloud compute networks subnetworks update prod-shared-vpc-us-east1 --region=us-east1 --enable-flow-logs), matching the configuration already present on prod-shared-vpc-us-central1.
